name: Greece
summary: Children, parents and the spouse are guaranteed half of their intestate share. A foreign resident can choose the law of their nationality (EU Succession Regulation art. 22). Greece has no trust law; foundations exist, but family use is unclear.
reserved_share: Descendants, parents, and the surviving spouse or registered partner who would inherit on intestacy: half of the intestate portion (Civil Code art. 1825; calculation arts. 1830-1834; lifetime gift clawback within two years, arts. 1835-1838; Law 3719/2008 art. 11).
foreign_law_note: EU Succession Regulation: the law of the last habitual residence applies by default (art. 21), but a resident foreign national may choose the law of their nationality (art. 22).
trust_note: Greece is not a party to the 1985 Hague Trusts Convention (not in the HCCH table). Greek law has no domestic trust; the tax code treats foreign trusts as taxable entities. Foundations are governed by Civil Code arts. 108-121 and Law 4182/2013; sources suggest private purposes are possible if specific, lasting and lawful, but this is unconfirmed.
open_questions: Whether a Greek foundation may serve private family purposes (Civil Code arts. 108-121, Law 4182/2013) was not confirmed.
Greek tax treatment of foreign trusts only taken from a Mondaq headline summary.
